rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the basmala, Allah is uniquely encompassing of perfection; al-Rahman gives existence through vast mercy and shows the accountable the path to salvation; al-Rahim chooses monotheists for divine intimacy and holiness.
rows.anchor: وسعت رحمة ايجاد كل مخلوق وأوضح للمكلفين طريق النجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura first appears to aim at affirming divine oneness, showing that unbelievers' worldly wealth and children cannot avail them, and urging pursuit of the Garden prepared for the God-fearing, whose traits recur throughout.
rows.anchor: المقاصد التي سيقت لها هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers treating tawhid as the sura's primary aim, since its other two aims follow from it; divine qayyumiyya entails just standing over every soul and requiting disobedience and obedience.
rows.anchor: وأحسن منه أن نخص القصد الأول وهو التوحيد بالقصد فيها فإن الأمرين الآخرين يرجعان إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura's placement follows the Fatiha's comprehensive summary: after the Book and the foundation of tawhid, the next sura calls people to unite on the established straight path.
rows.anchor: الكتاب المحيط بأمر الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Building on 2:21, this sura establishes God's oneness by showing that Jesus, despite reviving the dead, is God's servant; all are servants, so Surat al-Nisa then summons them to God and unity.
rows.anchor: فأثبت الوحدانيه له بأبطال إلهيه غيره بإثبات أن عيسى عليه السلام الذي كان يحيي الموتى عبده فغيره بطريق الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Al Imran fits the sura's tawhid aim: its evidence displays God's complete power, and tawhid is faith's highest degree and God's distinctive intelligible mark of sovereignty, bringing its bearer radiance; hence al-Zahra.
rows.anchor: ومما يدل على أن القصد بها هو التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Citing 8:29, he places the Furqan nearest the comprehensive Book: revelation has three ranks, the all-encompassing Book, the Furqan joining outward and inward, and Torah and Gospel, whose outward and inward aspects are related.
rows.anchor: فكان الفرقان أقرب الكتب للكتاب الجامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus's creation from a woman alone signals that increase has ended and the world nears its end; no Israelite prophet followed him, and the final prophet from another people came with the Hour, so the sura opens with oneness as God's sole dominion approaches.
rows.anchor: لما خلق عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام من أنثى فقط وهي أدنى أسباب النماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam's creation from fertile, dominant soil, and from the male as the stronger reproductive cause, signifies multiplying peoples; the sura that recounts Adam therefore opens with the Book, since proliferation calls for revealed laws and messengers.
rows.anchor: فصدر أول سورة ذكر فيها خلقه وابتداء أمره بالكتاب

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the opening of Al Imran points back to what the whole of al-Baqara established.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الزبير ما حاصله

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the Qur'an confirms earlier scripture and the already clarified straight path; after describing prior communities and Israelite resistance, this sura reports Torah and then Gospel as guidance for those granted success.
rows.anchor: أن الصراط المستقيم قد تبين شأنه لمن تقدم في كتبهم

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَيْهِ شَىْءٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse resumes the knowledge affirmed in the Throne Verse and demonstrates qayyumiyya, refuting claims that Jesus is divine; God's knowing the obedient and disobedient confirms that His books guide.
rows.anchor: ثم قال توضيحا لما قدم في آية الكرسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth and heaven make God's unbounded knowledge concrete for instruction; no claimant of divinity for Jesus can claim such complete knowledge.
rows.anchor: ولما كان تقريب المعلومات بالمحسوسات أقيد في التعليم والبعد عن الخفاء قال وإن كان علمه سبحانه وتعالى لا يتقيد بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He contrasts divine omniscience with Gospel accounts in Mark and Luke where Jesus asks who touched him and is told he does not know; the author cites this as evidence against Jesus's divinity.
rows.anchor: بل في إنجيلهم الذي بين أظهرهم الآن في حدود السبعين والثمانمائة التصريح بأنه يخفي عليه بعض الأمور

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the verse to al-Baqara's detailed accounts of their deeds: could their actions be hidden from the One who formed them in wombs and sees what no one else sees?
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زبير : ثم أشار قوله تعالى : {

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A messenger” coordinates with an implied “reciting,” or is accusative through an implied “he makes him”; Jesus is sent to the Children of Israel with the Gospel.
rows.anchor: عطفا على ( تاليا ) المقدر

words: أَنِّى قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِـَٔايَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle of expectation introduces the sign because a messenger addresses his recipients directly and they expect a proof; “your Lord” recalls God's longstanding beneficence toward them.
rows.anchor: وكان من شأن الرسول مخاطبة المرسل إليهم وإقباله بجميع رسالته عليهم اتبعه ببيان الرسالة مقرونا بحرف التوقع

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines clay as water and earth matured to receive an imprint, and the bird's form as the arrangement of limbs perceived by sight, prepared for its intended function.
rows.anchor: هو متخمر الماء والتراب حيث يصير متهيئا لقبول وقع الصورة فيه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali glosses blowing as forcefully sending air from its source; the mention of the process prevents anyone supposing Jesus is truly the creator.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : من النفخ , وهو إرسال الهواء من منبعثه بقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi reads “طائرا,” describing the result as actually flying; the author notes that this makes the bird's realized motion explicit.
rows.anchor: طائرا بالفعل - كما في قراءة نافع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated permission removes doubt and attributes the miracle to God; the living bird recalls Adam created from dust and is even more astonishing, so Jesus's unusual birth must not lead to deification.
rows.anchor: أي بتمكين الملك الأعظم الذي له جميع صفات الكمال

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says “I heal” means complete release from disease, which weakens faculties and changes their ordinary natural actions; he explains akmah as loss of sight and leprosy as a disordered bodily complexion.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : من الإبراء وهو تمام التخلص من الداء

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali connects leprosy to an abnormal temperament and corrupted phlegm that weakens the body's power to transform it into its normal color.
rows.anchor: وقال الحرالي : البرص عبارة عن سور مزاج يحصل بسببه تكرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raising the dead restores souls to bodies; Jesus actually raised some, and his granted power over some proves the One who enabled him can raise all.
rows.anchor: لأن الذي أقدرني على البعض قادر على ذلك في الكل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, as reported by al-Quda'i, relates that the Prophet called a man's dead daughter from a valley by God's permission; she emerged and chose God after her parents embraced Islam. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: نقل القضاعي أن الحسن قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He points to the story at 2:260, a report that the Prophet restored Qatada ibn Diama's eye after an arrow dislodged it, and the account that God cured Uways al-Qarni's leprosy for his kindness to his mother; no grading is given.
rows.anchor: وقصة قتادة ابن دعامة في رده صلى الله عليه وسلم عينه بعد أن أصابها سهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because reviving the dead is a divine prerogative, Jesus explicitly disclaims independent divinity and attributes the deed to God's enabling; he then adds another disclosure from the unseen.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ذلك من أمر الإحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus reports unseen information about what people eat and store, although he did not witness it; the home is the most private and concealing dwelling.
rows.anchor: أي من الأخبار الجليلة من عالم الغيب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali derives iddikhar from dakhira, retaining something for later need; he distinguishes private saving for oneself from ihtikar, storing goods to profit in trade.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : من الادخار : افتعال من الدخرة

words: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs show Jesus is God's servant and chosen one, not divine: he attributes them to God and acts dependently, even through supplication; they benefit those who submit to God's power and can truly believe.
rows.anchor: أي أيها المشاهدون على أني عبد الله ومصطفاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the address shifting between singular and plural as forestalling two objections: that only a collective could see the sign, or that it benefits just one person rather than all recipients.
rows.anchor: وكذا جمع ثانيا قطعا لتعنت من قد يقول

words: وَمُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَىَّ مِنَ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Confirming what came before me” can attach to the implied state of “I came to you,” or to “with a sign” if the preposition is circumstantial rather than transitive.
rows.anchor: عطف على الحال المقدر منه تأكيدا لأنه عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus confirms the Torah revealed to Moses but abrogates some of its prescriptions to ease the burden; the precedence of Torah also points to its created status.
rows.anchor: لأن القبلية تقتضي العدم الذي هو صف المخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Dajjal comparison explains why Jesus repeats the sign statement: sound hadiths warn that the Dajjal performs miracles, including reviving a dead man, and claims divinity; Jesus's decisive proof is servanthood and the prophets' shared call to worship God alone.
rows.anchor: منها إحياء ميت ويدعى الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus closes by urging reverent fear of God, who owns all affairs, and obedience to himself in accepting the message; piety necessarily entails following the messenger.
rows.anchor: فإن التقوى مستلزمة لطاعة الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After repeated counsel toward piety, justice, and beneficence, including marital kindness, this verse renews the sura's opening call to piety; its syntax can also connect to the command to seek God's bounty in 4:32.
rows.anchor: الوصايا من أولها إلى هنا بنتيجة التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship means obeying the wholly perfect God, unlike anything else, with unalloyed obedience, humility, and submission through keeping commands and avoiding prohibitions.
rows.anchor: الذي له الكمال كله فلا يشبهه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is self-sufficient, He accepts only sincere worship; the prohibition reinforces the exclusive devotion implied by worshipping Him.
rows.anchor: ولما كان سبحانه غنيا لم يقبل إلا الخالص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After faith and the higher rank of ihsan in worship, the command turns to ihsan in human stewardship, beginning with parents who were the means of one's existence; their kindness is paired with God's oneness.
rows.anchor: فصار المأمور بذلك مخلصا في عبادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kinship ties are a central concern of the sura, so this command details and reinforces its opening counsel; the repeated preposition underscores relatives' added right through closeness.
rows.anchor: قال مفصلا لما ذكر أول السورة تأكيدا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orphans and the poor merit care even without known kinship; both are weak, and the orphan comes first because youth leaves the child unable to meet needs or seek help.
rows.anchor: أي وإن لم تكن رحمهم معروفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A related neighbor has two rights; an unrelated neighbor still deserves care because of daily proximity and the harm a bad neighbor can cause. He quotes a supplication seeking refuge from a bad resident neighbor, unlike a nomadic one who moves.
rows.anchor: أي الذي لا قرابة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion at one's side is someone close and associated through a matter that prolongs companionship.
rows.anchor: الملاصق المخالط في أمر من الأمور الموجبة لامتداد العشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wayfarer is a traveler made vulnerable by distance from home, few helpers, and loneliness.
rows.anchor: المسافر لغربته وقلة ناصره ووحشته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those under one's ownership means male and female slaves, and treating them well is a great act of obedience.
rows.anchor: فإن الإحسان إليهم طاعة عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He quotes a report that the Prophet's final words concerned prayer and those owned by one's right hand; no grading or source is supplied here.
rows.anchor: آخر ما تكلم به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الصلاة وماملكت أيمانكم

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ مُخْتَالًۭا فَخُورًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhtal is conceited, proud of appearance and gifts, contemptuous of others, ashamed of poor relatives, and unwilling to help weak neighbors; fakhuur excessively boasts and shuns the poor.
rows.anchor: متكبرا معجبا بنفسه متزينا بحليته مرائيا بام آتاه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arrogance and boastfulness over perishable possessions lead to miserliness from fear of losing them; “those who are miserly” includes withholding knowledge and similar things.
rows.anchor: يوقعون البخل بما حملهم من المتاع الفاني على الفخار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their urging people to be miserly expresses hostility to generosity; “people” may signal that they only influence low-minded folk, or that their ostentation implicitly drives others to miserliness.
rows.anchor: وفي التعبير بما هو من النوس إشارة

words: وَيَكْتُمُونَ مَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also hoard speech that could be shared without harm, deny God's favor, and display poverty despite what they received.
rows.anchor: وهو الشح بالكلام الذي لا يخشى نقصه وجحد النعمة وإظهار الافتقار

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: In a report from Abdullah ibn Masud in al-Bukhari, the Prophet asks him to recite Surat al-Nisa; when he reaches 4:41, the Prophet tells him to stop and weeps. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وفي التفسير من البخاري عن عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When witnesses stand, unbelievers will wish the earth leveled over them, burying them with no unevenness; they dread the shame of rebuke and punishment to come.
rows.anchor: ولا تكون كذلك إلا وقد غيبتهم واستوت بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will not be able to hide anything from God but will be exposed by their evil accounts and carry all their burdens, requited for concealing His signs and proofs in life.
rows.anchor: بل يفتضحون بسيء أخبارهم , ويحملون جميع أوزارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terrifying judgment scene makes sinners wish for nonexistence and prevents concealment; because salvation requires purity through faith and obedience, the discussion turns to worldly prayer and purification.
rows.anchor: لا ينجو فيه إلا من كان طاهر القلب والجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address means those who profess belief in the messengers and what they brought from God; the foremost duty is to avoid associating anything with Him.
rows.anchor: أقروا بالتصديق بالرسل وما أتوا به عن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Do not approach prayer” means do not enter the place where it is performed, much less perform the prayer itself.
rows.anchor: بأن لا تكونوا في موضعها فضلا عن أن تفعلوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intoxication means loss of reason through wine or another cause; weakened reason lets Satan prompt the tongue toward verbal shirk even while the heart remains faithful, a statement that will cause anguish at judgment.
rows.anchor: أي غائبو العقل من الخمر أو نحوها
